Lurt 0.1.0 is the first release: a light, fast Windows browser written in Rust, with a liquid-glass look.

**Download Lurt:** [Windows (lurt.exe)](https://github.com/ladroxd/Lurt/releases/download/v0.1.0/lurt.exe) · [SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/ladroxd/Lurt/releases/download/v0.1.0/lurt.exe.sha256)

No installer: download it and run it. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the app isn't signed; choose **More info → Run anyway**. Needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime, which Windows 10 and 11 already include.

## New

- **Glass interface.** A borderless window over a blurred backdrop, with translucent tabs and toolbar, rounded page corners and soft animations.
- **Dark, light or system theme.** Pick an accent color, roundness, and a compact one-row layout in Settings.
- **Control the transparency.** Background opacity goes from clear glass to solid, and window opacity fades the whole window, websites included, so you can see your desktop through it.
- **Opens instantly.** The window appears with a skeleton of the interface while the page engine starts, and a sleeping tab wakes up behind a blurred picture of how you left it instead of a white flash.
- **Light on memory.** About 6 MB to download; new and restored tabs cost nothing until you open them, and idle background tabs go to sleep.
- **Ad and tracker blocking.** Built in, with a per-page count on the shield button. Click it to see which domains were blocked and to turn blocking off for a site that breaks.
- **Bookmarks bar.** Your bookmarks and folders under the toolbar, in your order: drag to rearrange or into folders, drop links onto it, and open folders as menus. Ctrl+Shift+B shows or hides it.
- **History your way.** Search it, pick pages to delete, clear the last hour, day or week, or have Lurt delete old history automatically.
- **Open files.** Paste a file path into the address bar to open images, PDFs and HTML pages.
- **Settings in their own window.** The gear button opens a centered glass window with a section for everything, over a blurred view of your page, and a search box that jumps straight to any setting.
- **Your start page, your sites.** Add favourites with the + tile, and right-click any tile to pin, edit or remove it.
- **Import from Chrome and Google.** Bring in bookmarks (with their folders) and history from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi or Opera on your PC, or from a Google Takeout export.
- **Your Google account.** The account you are signed in to Google with shows at the top right, with sign out, switch and add account. Settings → Account shows what Lurt keeps on your PC and backs up your settings to a file.
- **Start over in one click.** Delete all browser data (history, bookmarks, passwords, cookies, settings and tabs) from Settings. If you're signed in to Google, Lurt signs you out first.
- **Privacy your way.** Settings → Privacy & trackers has Standard and Strict protection levels, eight filter lists to pick from (cookie banners, annoyances, malware, crypto miners and more), clean links without tracking tags, Global Privacy Control, fingerprint protection, HTTPS upgrades, Secure DNS, WebRTC IP protection, site permissions, and deleting your history or cookies when Lurt closes.
- **Private tabs.** Ctrl+Shift+N opens a tab with its own cookies and no history; everything is gone when you close your last private tab.
- **Downloads.** A downloads button with a progress ring, a panel to pause, resume, cancel and open files, and a full Downloads page (Ctrl+J) with search, your download folder, Save as, and rules per file type, like blocking .exe files.
- **Bookmark where you want.** The star (or Ctrl+D) saves the page and opens a card to rename it, pick its folder or make a new one.
- **Loading screens in the site's colors.** YouTube loads in a soft breathing red, Twitch in purple, with just the site's name.
- **Fewer processes.** Embedded frames share their page's process, about half the memory of before.
- **Saves passwords and form data.** Lurt offers to remember logins after you sign in once.
- **Mods.** Restyle the browser with your own CSS, and change any website with per-site CSS or JavaScript files.

## Good to know

- Passwords and signed-in sessions can't be copied over from Chrome, because Chrome encrypts them so only Chrome can read them.
- Google is the default search engine; change it in Settings → Browsing.
